cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Identify, Analyze, and Prioritize Business Continuity Requirements”, part “People”.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “the first goal of a BCP”?
options: The first goal of any BCP must be to ensure the safety of your data during and after an emergency.
The first goal of any BCP must be to ensure the safety of your people only during an emergency.
The first goal of any BCP must be to ensure the safety of your people during and after an emergency.
The first goal of any BCP must be to protect the profit of your company during and after an emergency.
options_why: Data matters, but the first goal is people.
The goal covers the time after the emergency too.
Profit is not the first goal. People are.
cards.answer: The first goal of any BCP must be to ensure the safety of your people during and after an emergency.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: first goal, safety of your people, during and after an emergency.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “the first goal of a BCP” from memory.
cards.answer: The first goal of any BCP must be to ensure the safety of your people during and after an emergency.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the first goal, the safety of your people, during and after an emergency.

cards.question: Official definition: “people in a continuity plan”
cards.answer: People are always, without exception, your most valuable and critical asset.
cards.explanation: In simple words: an asset is a thing of value. People are the most valuable asset, without any exception.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Identify, Analyze, and Prioritize Business Continuity Requirements”, part “People”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “people in a continuity plan” from memory.
cards.answer: People are always, without exception, your most valuable and critical asset.
cards.explanation: Three parts: always without exception, most valuable, critical asset.

cards.question: Official definition: “the BCP itself”
cards.answer: The BCP itself is the organization's commitment to maintaining the operations of the business, and the steps the organization takes to do so.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the plan is a promise from the company to keep working, with the steps to keep that promise.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Identify, Analyze, and Prioritize Business Continuity Requirements”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “the BCP itself” from memory.
cards.answer: The BCP itself is the organization's commitment to maintaining the operations of the business, and the steps the organization takes to do so.
cards.explanation: Three parts: the organization's commitment, maintaining the operations, the steps it takes.

cards.question: Official definition: “the scope of the BCP”
cards.answer: The scope of the BCP must encompass all of the organization's operations, including each business area and within every geographic region that the organization does business.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the scope says how far the plan goes. It goes everywhere in the company.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Identify, Analyze, and Prioritize Business Continuity Requirements”. To encompass means to include everything.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “the scope of the BCP” from memory.
cards.answer: The scope of the BCP must encompass all of the organization's operations, including each business area and within every geographic region that the organization does business.
cards.explanation: Three parts: all operations, each business area, every geographic region.

cards.question: In which order does a BCP deal with its three families?
options: People, then processes, then technologies
Technologies first, then processes, then people
Processes, then people, then technologies
Technologies, then people, then processes
options_why: This order is reversed. People come first.
People come before processes in the manual.
People come first, not last.
cards.answer: People, then processes, then technologies
cards.explanation: A machine can be replaced, but a person cannot. So people come first.

cards.question: What is the first goal of a BCP?
options: Saving the backups of the customer data
The safety of people in an emergency
Keeping the website online for customers
Warning the press and the public about it
options_why: Data matters, but people matter more.
The website matters, but it comes after people.
Public news is useful later, but it is not the first goal.
cards.answer: The safety of people in an emergency
cards.explanation: Before the data and the machines, we protect people.

cards.question: Which people does a continuity plan cover?
options: Only the employees who have a contract with the company
Only the technical team that runs the recovery
Only the managers who take the decisions
Anyone the event can affect, like customers
options_why: The manual also lists contractors, customers, and vendors.
The technical team is only a small part of the people concerned.
Managers are only a part of the people concerned.
cards.answer: Anyone the event can affect, like customers
cards.explanation: The manual lists employees, contractors, customers, vendors, and any other person who may be affected.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “People”.

cards.question: After the safety of people, what must the plan give them?
cards.answer: The resources to keep working almost normally, like shelter (an alternate work site) and food.
cards.explanation: People who are safe must also be able to work.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “People”.

cards.question: A fire starts in the office of a company. What should the plan protect FIRST?
options: The people in the building
The servers in the data room
The backups of the customer files
The public image of the brand
options_why: Servers can be replaced. People cannot.
Backups matter, but they come after people.
Image matters later. People come first.
cards.answer: The people in the building
cards.explanation: The first goal of any BCP is the safety of people.

cards.question: A company works in three countries, but its plan covers only one. What is the BEST way to fix this?
options: Keep the plan, because most staff work in one country
Ask each other country to write its own plan alone
Widen the scope to every region where it works
Wait to see if a disaster happens in the other countries
options_why: The other two countries would stay without protection.
Separate plans with no link may leave gaps. The scope must cover all operations.
A plan should exist before a disaster, not after it.
cards.answer: Widen the scope to every region where it works
cards.explanation: The scope must encompass all operations, every business area, and every region.

cards.question: Which task MOST clearly belongs to the processes family?
options: Warning the employees about the event
Making backups of the data
Renting two internet providers
Making sure critical supplies keep arriving
options_why: Warning people belongs to the people family.
Backups belong to the technologies family.
Internet providers belong to the technologies family.
cards.answer: Making sure critical supplies keep arriving
cards.explanation: Processes are the ways of working, like supplies and the choice of where to process data.

cards.question: Why does a BCP put people before technologies?
cards.answer: A machine can be replaced. A person cannot, and nothing restarts without people.
cards.explanation: Machines are useful only if people can run them.

cards.question: Which task belongs to the technologies family?
options: Planning a shelter for the staff
Making backups of the systems
Making sure critical supplies keep arriving
Keeping managers informed
options_why: A shelter is for people.
Supplies are a process.
Informing managers is part of the people family.
cards.answer: Making backups of the systems
cards.explanation: Technologies are the systems and tools, like backups and redundant systems.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT usually in the scope of a BCP?
options: A communications plan
BCP testing requirements
A plan for a new ad campaign
Threats, vulnerabilities, and risks
options_why: A communications plan is in the scope.
Tests are in the scope.
Threats and risks are in the scope.
cards.answer: A plan for a new ad campaign
cards.explanation: The scope of most plans covers critical functions, risks, backups, personnel, communication, and tests.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, scope of the BCP.

cards.question: Who should BEST receive regular updates during a disaster?
options: Management and the key BCP people
Only the IT department
Only the staff in the damaged building
Nobody, until the disaster ends
options_why: The IT department is only a part of the people who decide.
Other people also need news to take decisions.
Without news, leaders cannot decide well during the disaster.
cards.answer: Management and the key BCP people
cards.explanation: Regular updates allow well-informed decisions.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “People”.

cards.question: How far must the scope of the BCP go?
cards.answer: It must cover all operations, every business area, and every region where the company works.
cards.explanation: A region that is not covered is a hole in the plan.

cards.question: Why does the plan list several ways to warn the key staff? Which reason is BEST?
options: Staff prefer different apps
One way may fail during the disaster
One way is cheaper than all the others
A law requires exactly three ways
options_why: Habits are not the reason. The goal is to stay reachable.
Cost is not the reason in the manual.
The manual does not give such a law.
cards.answer: One way may fail during the disaster
cards.explanation: If one way fails, another must still work. Otherwise important people would not hear the news.

cards.question: Name two things that the scope of most BCPs includes.
cards.answer: For example: critical business functions, threats and risks, data backup and recovery, BCP staff, communication, and tests.
cards.explanation: The manual lists six items.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, scope of the BCP.

paragraphes: A storm floods the rooms of your school. Lessons cannot happen there for weeks.
The town hall lends its big hall. The grades exist in two copies: one at the school and one at the town hall.
Three things saved the school: another place, copies of its documents, and spare suppliers. A continuity plan prepares these things.

decouverte.comme: You keep a spare set of keys with a neighbor. If you lose yours, you can still get in. But if the spare set is inside your house, it is useless when the house burns.
decouverte.enVrai: A backup is a copy of the data. To be useful, it must be kept away from the main site. This is called offsite. In the cloud (computers that you rent over the internet), copies are kept in several regions. A region is a place in the world where data centers are. The image stops here: a company keeps several copies, not just one.

decouverte.question: A company keeps its backup copies in the room next to its server. A fire destroys the building. What happens to the copies?
options: They disappear with the server
They survive, because they are copies
The firefighters protect them
decouverte.explanation: A copy kept in the same place suffers the same disaster. This is why the manual asks for copies away from the site.

decouverte.texte: A company rents two internet service providers (ISP, the companies that supply internet). It also has several power suppliers and two banks. If one fails, another takes over. Having a double of what you depend on is called redundancy.

A recovery site is another place to work when the main place is lost. A hot site is ready to use right away, with the equipment in place. A cold site is an empty room, and you must bring everything. A warm site is in between. This comparison comes from outside the manual.

cards.question: Official definition: “types of recovery sites”
cards.answer: The primary recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.
cards.explanation: In simple words: a recovery site is another place to work if the main place is lost. There are three kinds: hot, cold, and warm.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “Processes”. The manual gives details in chapter 7.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “types of recovery sites”?
options: The primary recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and mobile sites.
The primary recover site types are hot sites, cool sites, and warm sites.
The only recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.
The primary recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.
options_why: Mobile site is not one of the three types in the sentence.
Cool site is not a type. The three types are hot, cold, and warm.
The word only is not in the sentence.
cards.answer: The primary recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.
cards.explanation: Look at the key words: primary, hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “types of recovery sites” from memory.
cards.answer: The primary recover site types are hot sites, cold sites, and warm sites.
cards.explanation: Three words to remember: hot, cold, warm.

cards.question: Official definition: “an essential BCP process”
cards.answer: One of the most essential BCP processes assures an organization that its critical data processing facilities and capabilities remain operational during a disaster.
cards.explanation: In simple words: the company must keep processing its critical data, even if the main site is hit.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “Processes”.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “an essential BCP process” from memory.
cards.answer: One of the most essential BCP processes assures an organization that its critical data processing facilities and capabilities remain operational during a disaster.
cards.explanation: Three parts: critical data processing facilities, remain operational, during a disaster.

cards.question: Where must at least one set of backups be kept?
options: Away from the main site
In the same room as the server
On the desk of the IT manager
On the main server itself
options_why: A fire in the room would destroy the server and the copies together.
A desk in the same building has the same risks.
A copy on the same server is lost when the server is lost.
cards.answer: Away from the main site
cards.explanation: A copy kept away from the site survives the disaster that hits the site.

cards.question: What is redundancy?
options: Making a full copy of the data every single day
Keeping the data secret from outside people
Having a double of what we depend on
Removing old files to save storage space
options_why: That describes a backup. Redundancy doubles the means, such as power and internet.
That describes confidentiality, a different idea.
Cleaning files does not protect the business in a disaster.
cards.answer: Having a double of what we depend on
cards.explanation: If one supplier fails, the other one takes over.

cards.question: A company rents two internet providers. Which idea is this?
options: A backup of the data
A hot site
An offsite copy
Redundancy
options_why: A backup copies data. A second provider doubles a service.
A hot site is a ready place to work, not a service.
An offsite copy is data kept away from the main site.
cards.answer: Redundancy
cards.explanation: Two providers means a double of the means. If one fails, the other works.

cards.question: Where must at least one set of backups be kept for a company with its own data center?
cards.answer: Offsite: away from the main site, in case a disaster destroys it.
cards.explanation: A copy kept outside survives the disaster that hits the site.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “Technologies”.

cards.question: A company stores its data in the cloud, which means in computers that it rents over the internet. What is the BEST way to keep the data recoverable?
options: Keep a single copy in the cheapest region
Keep copies in several cloud regions
Do nothing, because the cloud never fails
Keep all the copies in the same data center
options_why: One region is a weak point. A disaster there would lose the data.
The cloud can fail too. You need copies.
If that data center is hit, the original and the copies disappear together.
cards.answer: Keep copies in several cloud regions
cards.explanation: With several regions, the data can be recovered at any time.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “Technologies”.

cards.question: A company has its own data center. Which backup plan is MOST in line with the manual?
options: One copy, kept in the data center only
Several copies, all kept in the data center
Several copies, with one set stored offsite
Copies kept only on the laptops of the IT team
options_why: One copy is a weak point, and it is in the same place as the data.
A disaster at the data center would destroy all of them.
Laptops are not a safe place for the copies of the whole company.
cards.answer: Several copies, with one set stored offsite
cards.explanation: The manual says to keep several copies, and one set must be stored offsite.

cards.question: A storm cuts the power of the server building. The company keeps working because of a second power supplier. Which idea did it use?
options: Redundancy
Offsite backup
Staff training
Role-based access
options_why: An offsite backup protects data, not the power supply.
Training helps people, but it does not supply power.
Access control decides who can see data. It does not supply power.
cards.answer: Redundancy
cards.explanation: A second supplier doubles the means that the company depends on.

cards.question: Why do companies rent two internet service providers?
cards.answer: If one fails, the other keeps the company connected. The problem may come from the provider, not from the company.
cards.explanation: A single provider is a weak point.

cards.question: Which choice carries the LEAST risk if one provider fails?
options: One internet provider with a long contract
Two internet providers
One internet provider with great support
One very fast internet provider
options_why: A long contract does not help if the provider fails.
Good support cannot bring back a failed line quickly enough.
Speed does not help if the one provider fails.
cards.answer: Two internet providers
cards.explanation: With two providers, the second one keeps the company connected.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a good protection against hardware failure?
options: Making full backups of systems and data
Storing one set of backups offsite
Having redundant power and network supplies
Keeping the only backup near the server
options_why: Backups are the most proven way to face failures.
An offsite set survives a disaster at the site.
Redundant supplies keep the company working if one fails.
cards.answer: Keeping the only backup near the server
cards.explanation: A backup next to the server suffers the same disaster as the server.

cards.question: A company wants a backup site with equipment that is ready to use right away. Which kind of site is this?
options: A hot site
A cold site
A warm site
A remote site
options_why: A cold site is only an empty room. You must bring the equipment.
A warm site is in between: it has some of the equipment.
Remote site is not one of the three types.
cards.answer: A hot site
cards.explanation: A hot site is ready to use now. This is the fastest way to restart.
cards.explanation_more: Outside the manual: chapter 7 gives details. Hot means ready now, warm means partly ready, and cold means an empty room.

cards.question: Name two supplies that a company should double for a disaster.
cards.answer: For example: electricity, water, telecommunications, and network connections.
cards.explanation: The manual asks for redundant supplies.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, part “Technologies”.

cards.question: What is the most proven way to face hardware and software failures?
cards.answer: Backups of the systems and the data. The manual calls them the most tried-and-true way.
cards.explanation: Failures are a normal part of technology.

cards.question: What is a cold site compared with a hot site?
cards.answer: A cold site is an empty room: you must bring all the equipment. A hot site is ready to use right away.
cards.explanation: A warm site is in between.
cards.explanation_more: Outside the manual: chapter 7 gives details about hot, warm, and cold sites.
